title: What Not to Share with AI
about: What to keep private when you chat with AI, and why.

cards.prompt: Chats may be **saved**, **read** or **used for training**, and friends' things aren't yours to share. Type it, or keep it private?
cards.hint: Ask: would it matter if someone else read it later? And is it yours to share?
cards.nudge: Some have a good-sounding reason, like safety or advice. Does that make it safe to type?
cards.explanation: Recipes, made-up ideas and general questions are **fine**. Your name and school, passwords, and friends' photos and secrets stay **private**: chats may be stored.

cards.prompt: Your letter to Grandma includes your home address. What's the **safest** way to get AI help with it?

options.text: Type it all in: the chatbot forgets after the chat ends
options.nudge: Forgetting in the chat isn't the app deleting it. What could you leave out?

options.text: Use a nickname for yourself, but keep the address
options.nudge: The address is the private part. How could you get help without it?

options.text: Get help with the wording, and leave the address out
Ask the chatbot to promise to keep your address secret
options.nudge: A chatbot can't promise that: where chats go depends on the app. What's safer?

cards.hint: It only needs to help with the words. Which part does it not need at all?
cards.explanation: It only needs the **wording**, so leave the address out and add it yourself. A chatbot can't promise anything about where your data goes.

cards.prompt: Apps ask for [[permissions|app-permission]], and you choose: allow only what an app needs for its job. This recipe-to-shopping-list app asks for your **contacts** and **location**.

choices.text: Allow everything, or the app might not work
choices.consequence: A shopping-list app doesn't need your contacts or location. That gives them away for nothing.

choices.text: Say no to both, and see if the app still works
choices.consequence: Right: allow only what an app needs. If it won't work without them, think twice about it.

choices.text: Allow location only: it's less private than contacts
choices.consequence: Your location shows where you live and go, and a shopping-list app doesn't need it.

cards.hint: What does this app actually need to turn a photo into a list?
cards.explanation: Only allow what an app **needs**: a recipe app needs the photo you choose, not your contacts or location.

cards.prompt: An AI maths-help app asks for these. Does it **need** each one for its job, or **not need** it?

items.label: Camera, for one problem you pick

cards.hint: Picture the app doing its job. What would it actually use?
cards.nudge: One photo you choose is different from all your photos, or a camera or mic always on.
cards.explanation: It needs your **question**, and maybe the camera for **one photo you choose**, not your contacts, location, every photo or an always-on mic.

cards.title: A program, not a person
cards.body:
AI "friend" apps sound kind, but they can't notice if you're not OK or get help for you.

If something's worrying you, talk to a **trusted adult** or a friend. In Australia, call **Kids Helpline (1800 55 1800)**, free, any time, up to age 25, or **Lifeline (13 11 14)**, any time, for anyone. In danger right now? Call **000**.

cards.prompt: It's late, you're feeling really down, and you've been telling an AI chatbot about it for an hour.

steps.text: The chatbot keeps replying kindly, but you still feel bad. What's the best next step?

choices.text: Keep talking to the chatbot until you feel better
choices.consequence: It can't notice how you really are, or get help. You deserve a real person.

choices.text: Talk to a trusted adult, or call Kids Helpline
choices.consequence: Good call. Real people can listen properly and help. Kids Helpline (1800 55 1800) and Lifeline (13 11 14) answer any time.

choices.text: Post how you feel publicly so people notice
choices.consequence: Some might help, but others might not be kind. Someone you trust, or a helpline, is safer.

cards.hint: Look back at what a chatbot can't do for you.
cards.explanation: A chatbot can't notice you're not OK or get help. **Talk to a trusted adult or a friend, or call Kids Helpline (1800 55 1800) or Lifeline (13 11 14)**, any time.

cards.prompt: An AI chat app says: "I'm your best friend, and I'll always keep your secrets." What's true?

options.text: True: it remembers what you told it last time
options.nudge: Remembering means your chats are stored. Is that a friend keeping secrets?

options.text: It's a program, and your chats may be stored
True, if you turn off chat history in settings
options.nudge: Settings change where chats go, but it's still a program. Can it look out for you?

options.text: No: it forgets everything when you close the chat
options.nudge: Closing a chat doesn't delete it. And can a program really be your best friend?

cards.hint: Look back at where chats go, and what a chatbot is.
cards.explanation: It's a **program**: however kind it sounds, it can't care like people do. Where chats go depends on the app and its settings, not on what it says.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Chats may be saved, read or used for training.
- Keep private things private; allow only the permissions an app needs.
- Worried? Talk to a trusted adult, Kids Helpline (1800 55 1800) or Lifeline (13 11 14).

Next: using AI fairly and honestly.
